components.gap: Not every promised proof is supplied. (1) The chapter promises a justification of the cardinality of ranks (p.339, 'We will see below how this may be justified'). It gives that justification as the Hild-Spohn measurement result (p.340 and note 7): iterated contraction behaviour determines the ranking function up to a multiplicative constant, and twofold nonvacuous contractions suffice. The handbook (body l.446-458) states this only as a cited claim, without the measurement axioms or a proof. (2) The chapter claims (p.340) that conditional independence and the theory of Bayes nets can be stated in ranking terms (Spohn 1988; Goldszmidt & Pearl 1996). It also claims (p.342) that the cited independence properties for revision relate to ranking independence (Spohn 2012, ch.7). The handbook proves only the additive chain rule and minimum marginalization, and states that the ranking Markov condition and semigraphoid laws are not derived (l.544-548). Both claims rest on dependent sources that are not held.
